skill.name: tmux
skill.description: Manage tmux sessions for long-running terminal processes and interactive command workflows.
skill.summary: Control tmux sessions, send commands, capture output, and clean up terminal processes.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: The static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, and shell examples in SKILL.md. Semantic review found that the skill intentionally controls tmux sessions, sends arbitrary terminal commands, and captures raw pane output, which requires user confirmation and careful handling.

remediation.issue: The skill can send arbitrary commands to tmux sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before creating sessions with commands or sending commands that modify files, access secrets, or affect services.

remediation.issue: Captured tmux output may contain sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before displaying captured output and avoid storing or reusing terminal content that may include secrets.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples include broad terminal automation without safety boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to verify target sessions, working directories, and commands before execution.

static_findings.snippet: - [tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux) installed (`brew install tmux` or `apt install tmux`)
- `--command <cmd>` - Initial command to run in the session
- `--literal` - Send keys literally (no special key interpretation)
- `--lines <n>` - Number of lines of scrollback to capture (default: 100)
- `--wait <pattern>` - Wait for output matching this pattern before capturing
- Use `--json` for structured output when parsing programmatically
- Session names should be descriptive and unique (e.g., `psql-mydb`, `logs-app`)
- [tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux) installed (`brew install tmux` or `apt install tmux`)

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Terminal Command Control
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents options that create tmux sessions with user-provided commands and send commands to existing sessions. This can execute destructive local commands if an agent uses untrusted instructions without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly defines command inputs for session creation and command sending. The risk follows directly from the intended terminal-control capability.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Terminal Output Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The capture workflow returns raw terminal content from tmux panes. That output may include credentials, database rows, logs, or other sensitive data visible in a session.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented capture command reads pane scrollback and returns raw terminal content. Sensitive exposure depends on what the user or agent ran in the session.

content.value_statement: Long-running terminal work is hard to supervise from a single command. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code manage tmux sessions, send commands, and read results.
actual_capabilities: Lists active tmux sessions and supports structured output.
Creates tmux sessions with optional command, working directory, and window name.
Sends commands or special key sequences to a selected session target.
Captures pane output with line limits, wait patterns, and timeouts.
Terminates named tmux sessions when work is complete.
Supports database, log monitoring, and REPL workflows.
limitations: Requires Bun and tmux to be installed on the host machine.
Can only manage sessions available to the current system user.
Does not prove that a command is safe before it is sent.
Captured output may include raw terminal formatting and sensitive content.

use_cases.title: Monitor Application Logs
use_cases.description: Start a persistent log session, inspect recent output, and stop the session after investigation.

use_cases.title: Work With Database Consoles
use_cases.description: Keep a database shell open, send selected queries, and capture the results for review.

use_cases.title: Run Interactive Analysis
use_cases.description: Control a Python or Node REPL across multiple steps without losing process state.

prompt_templates.title: List Active Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the active tmux sessions and summarize which ones look relevant to my current task.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Log Monitor
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a background process for operational debugging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tmux session for application logs, capture the first useful output, and leave the session running.

prompt_templates.title: Drive a Database Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Use an existing interactive database shell.
prompt_templates.prompt: Send a safe read-only query to my database tmux session, wait for the prompt, and capture the result.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Stateful REPL
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with multiple terminal steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a tmux REPL session to run a short analysis, capture each result, and clean up the session when finished.

output: Reports the session names, target identifiers, and visible status.
Notes when no tmux sessions are available.

output_examples.input: Capture the latest output from the log session.
output: Returns recent terminal output from the selected pane.
Highlights whether the requested wait pattern appeared before timeout.

output_examples.output: Confirms that the named tmux session was terminated or explains why it was not found.

best_practices: Confirm commands before sending them to sessions that can change files or services.
Use clear session names that identify the project, task, or environment.
Kill temporary sessions after work is complete to avoid stale processes.
anti_patterns: Sending commands from untrusted text without user approval.
Capturing and sharing terminal output that may contain secrets.
Reusing vague session names across unrelated projects.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages tmux sessions used for long-running or interactive terminal processes.

faq.question: Does it install tmux or Bun?
faq.answer: No. The host machine must already have tmux and Bun installed.

faq.question: Can it run any command?
faq.answer: It can send user-provided commands to tmux sessions, so users should approve sensitive actions first.

faq.question: Can it read command output?
faq.answer: Yes. It can capture raw pane output from a selected tmux session.

faq.question: Does it support structured output?
faq.answer: The documented commands include JSON output options for programmatic parsing.

faq.question: When should sessions be killed?
faq.answer: Temporary sessions should be killed when the task is complete or when the process is no longer needed.
